investigation.title: Remote Agent Creation Blocked by Swarm Agent Quota Limit (409 Conflict: agent quota exceeded: limit is 100)
investigation.summary: All three remote-agents eval checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed at 2026-06-16T18:01:29–32Z with an identical 409 Conflict response from POST /api/agents: the swarm backend rejected the creation request because the org-scoped remote agent quota of 100 has been reached. Because the agent creation call failed immediately, no evidence (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) was ever collected, causing the expected-output contract to be fully unmet.
investigation.rootCause: The production swarm backend returned HTTP 409 with error code "conflict" and message "conflict: agent quota exceeded: limit is 100" when the eval runner called POST /api/agents to create a remote agent. The quota ceiling of 100 remote agents for the eval org has been reached, so the creation request is rejected before any agent lifecycle state can be observed. This is a backend resource-limit condition on the POST /api/agents endpoint, not an eval infrastructure misconfiguration. All three sibling checks share the identical failure message, confirming the block occurs at the shared agent-creation step that all three checks depend on.

possibleCauses: [Most likely] The eval org's remote agent count has reached the swarm backend hard limit of 100. Previous eval runs created agents that were not cleaned up (e.g., due to prior failures in the withCleanup path), causing quota exhaustion over time.

[Possible] A prior eval run crashed or was interrupted before the withCleanup teardown could delete the agent it created, leaving a leaked agent that counts against the quota. Repeated occurrences accumulate until the limit is hit.
[Less likely] The quota limit of 100 was recently lowered by a backend configuration change, causing previously-passing runs to suddenly exceed the new ceiling.
[Less likely] The eval org is shared with non-eval workloads that independently consumed remote agent quota, leaving insufficient headroom for the probe to create a new agent.

investigation.title: Remote Agents eval suite blocked by swarm agent quota exhaustion (HTTP 409) on POST /api/agents
investigation.summary: All three remote-agents checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed at 2026-06-16T18:01:30–32Z with an identical HTTP 409 response from POST /api/agents indicating the swarm backend rejected agent creation because the org-scoped agent quota of 100 has been reached. Because the eval runner calls createAgent as its first step (infra/evals/status/run-status-probes.mjs line 1359), no agent was ever created, so zero required evidence fields (orgId, agentId, readyState, state) were collected and the expected-output contract was fully unmet.
investigation.rootCause: The swarm backend returned HTTP 409 conflict with the message "conflict: agent quota exceeded: limit is 100" on every POST /api/agents call made by the eval probe account or org. Because agent creation is the prerequisite first step for all three remote-agents checks, every downstream check in the suite failed before any evidence could be gathered. This is a shared upstream dependency failure localized to the POST /api/agents endpoint for the probe org, not a code defect in the eval runner itself.

verifierContext.siblingCorrelation.likelySharedDependencyFailure: true — all failing sibling IDs share the same message
possibleCauses: Primary (high confidence): The eval probe org has accumulated 100 or more live remote agents from previous eval runs that were not cleaned up, causing the swarm quota to be exhausted. The withCleanup wrapper in the runner (infra/evals/status/run-status-probes.mjs) may have failed to delete agents from prior runs, leaving them counted against the quota.

Secondary (medium confidence): The swarm service enforces a hard per-org limit of 100 agents and the probe org's quota was consumed by non-eval workloads or a cleanup regression, leaving no capacity for new eval agents.

Tertiary (low confidence): The quota limit itself was recently lowered on the swarm side, causing previously passing runs to now exceed the threshold. No source evidence supports a quota-limit change, so this remains speculative.

investigation.summary: All three remote-agents eval checks (remote-agent-runtime, remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state) failed at 2026-06-16T18:01:30–32Z with an identical 409 conflict response from POST /api/agents indicating the swarm agent quota of 100 has been reached for the eval org. investigation.rootCause: The production-api swarm backend rejected every POST /api/agents call with HTTP 409 and the message "conflict: agent quota exceeded: limit is 100". Because the eval runner calls createAgent as its first substantive step (run-status-probes.mjs:1372), the 409 terminates execution before any evidence is gathered, causing all three sibling checks to fail with the same error. This is a shared upstream dependency failure localized to the swarm agent-creation endpoint for the eval org, not a broad service outage. No user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence; this is an eval infrastructure failure.

investigation.title: Image Generation Stream Eval Failure: SESSION_OPEN_FAILED (404) on production-api Runtime — Agent Harness Unreachable
investigation.summary: The image-generation-stream eval for the production-api runtime environment failed immediately (latencyMs=2078) with a SESSION_OPEN_FAILED error carrying a 404 status, indicating the agent runtime harness endpoint targeted by the eval runner was unreachable or returned a not-found response. The identical check passed on the desktop-release runtime (latencyMs=127349, imageUrlPresent=true, generation_completed frame present), confirming the failure is localized to the production-api harness endpoint and is not a shared upstream image generation service outage.
investigation.rootCause: The eval runner called /api/generate/image/stream against the production-api runtime environment and received a 404 before any image generation work could begin. The stream emitted generation_start followed immediately by generation_error with code SESSION_OPEN_FAILED, meaning the agent runtime session could not be opened because the harness endpoint was not found at the configured URL (LOCAL_HARNESS_URL / SWARM_BASE_URL). This is an eval infrastructure connectivity failure scoped to the production-api harness target, not a user-facing image generation outage. The desktop-release sibling check passed with a full generation_completed frame sequence and a valid image URL, ruling out a problem with the image generation service itself.
proof: failed-check.evidence: generation_error frame carries code=SESSION_OPEN_FAILED and message='agent runtime endpoint not found (404): the harness is unreachable or running an incompatible version.'

investigations.title: Remote Agent Creation Blocked by Swarm Agent Quota Limit (409 Conflict: agent quota exceeded: limit is 100)
investigations.summary: All three remote-agents eval checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed at 2026-06-16T18:01:29–32Z with an identical 409 Conflict response from POST /api/agents: the swarm backend rejected the creation request because the org-scoped remote agent quota of 100 has been reached. Because the agent creation call failed immediately, no evidence (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) was ever collected, causing the expected-output contract to be fully unmet.
investigations.rootCause: The production swarm backend returned HTTP 409 with error code "conflict" and message "conflict: agent quota exceeded: limit is 100" when the eval runner called POST /api/agents to create a remote agent. The quota ceiling of 100 remote agents for the eval org has been reached, so the creation request is rejected before any agent lifecycle state can be observed. This is a backend resource-limit condition on the POST /api/agents endpoint, not an eval infrastructure misconfiguration. All three sibling checks share the identical failure message, confirming the block occurs at the shared agent-creation step that all three checks depend on.

possibleCauses: [Most likely] The eval org's remote agent count has reached the swarm backend hard limit of 100. Previous eval runs created agents that were not cleaned up (e.g., due to prior failures in the withCleanup path), causing quota exhaustion over time.

[Possible] A prior eval run crashed or was interrupted before the withCleanup teardown could delete the agent it created, leaving a leaked agent that counts against the quota. Repeated occurrences accumulate until the limit is hit.
[Less likely] The quota limit of 100 was recently lowered by a backend configuration change, causing previously-passing runs to suddenly exceed the new ceiling.
[Less likely] The eval org is shared with non-eval workloads that independently consumed remote agent quota, leaving insufficient headroom for the probe to create a new agent.

investigations.rootCause: The swarm backend returned HTTP 409 conflict with the message "conflict: agent quota exceeded: limit is 100" on every POST /api/agents call made by the eval probe account or org. Because agent creation is the prerequisite first step for all three remote-agents checks, every downstream check in the suite failed before any evidence could be gathered. This is a shared upstream dependency failure localized to the POST /api/agents endpoint for the probe org, not a code defect in the eval runner itself.

If the quota is legitimately exhausted by non-eval agents, coordinate with the team owning the eval org to either raise the swarm quota limit or isolate the eval org from production agent workloads.

Monitor the remote-agent-create and remote-agent-state checks (both marked required=true in features.json) as the primary signal for this failure class, since they are the required checks that gate feature health status.

investigations.title: Image Generation Stream Eval Failure: SESSION_OPEN_FAILED (404) on production-api Runtime — Agent Harness Unreachable
investigations.summary: The image-generation-stream eval for the production-api runtime environment failed immediately (latencyMs=2078) with a SESSION_OPEN_FAILED error carrying a 404 status, indicating the agent runtime harness endpoint targeted by the eval runner was unreachable or returned a not-found response. The identical check passed on the desktop-release runtime (latencyMs=127349, imageUrlPresent=true, generation_completed frame present), confirming the failure is localized to the production-api harness endpoint and is not a shared upstream image generation service outage.
investigations.rootCause: The eval runner called /api/generate/image/stream against the production-api runtime environment and received a 404 before any image generation work could begin. The stream emitted generation_start followed immediately by generation_error with code SESSION_OPEN_FAILED, meaning the agent runtime session could not be opened because the harness endpoint was not found at the configured URL (LOCAL_HARNESS_URL / SWARM_BASE_URL). This is an eval infrastructure connectivity failure scoped to the production-api harness target, not a user-facing image generation outage. The desktop-release sibling check passed with a full generation_completed frame sequence and a valid image URL, ruling out a problem with the image generation service itself.
proof: failed-check.evidence: generation_error frame carries code=SESSION_OPEN_FAILED and message='agent runtime endpoint not found (404): the harness is unreachable or running an incompatible version.'

failed-check.message: both contract assertions failed — frameTypes did not contain 'generation_completed' and imageUrlPresent was false — as a direct consequence of the 404 aborting the stream before any generation frames were emitted.
failed-check.timing: latencyMs=2078 is far below the warningLatencyMs=180000 threshold, consistent with an immediate connection failure rather than a slow or partial generation.

sibling.image-generation-stream: the same check on runtimeEnvironment=desktop-release passed with status=pass, imageUrlPresent=true, and a frameTypes sequence that includes generation_completed, proving the image generation service and eval contract are sound.

source-context.infra/evals/status/run-status-probes.mjs:1431-1439: the runner calls apiSse(args, '/api/generate/image/stream', ...) using the configured harness base URL, which is the endpoint that returned 404.
source.check-config.image-generation-stream: the production-api check is registered as required=false with statusImpact=informational, so this failure does not constitute a declared service outage.
possibleCauses: The production-api harness (LOCAL_HARNESS_URL or SWARM_BASE_URL) was not deployed, was down, or was pointing to a URL where the /api/generate/image/stream route does not exist at the time the eval ran — most likely cause given the immediate 404 and SESSION_OPEN_FAILED error.
The harness is running an incompatible version that no longer exposes the expected endpoint path, as stated verbatim in the error message from failed-check.evidence.
The SWARM_BASE_URL or LOCAL_HARNESS_URL environment variable was misconfigured or empty for the production-api eval run, causing the runner to target a wrong or default URL that returns 404.
A recent deployment to the production-api harness removed or renamed the /api/generate/image/stream route, making it unreachable for this eval environment only.

Confirm the /api/generate/image/stream SSE route is present and responding on the production-api harness; if it was removed or renamed, restore or update the route registration.

If the harness was intentionally not deployed for the production-api environment, update the check registration in infra/evals/status/features.json to reflect the correct runtimeEnvironment or mark the check as skipped until the harness is available.

Note that this check is registered as required=false with statusImpact=informational (source.check-config.image-generation-stream), so no status page impact is expected; however, the failure should be resolved to maintain eval coverage for the production-api image generation path.

whatWouldDisproveThis: A successful HTTP response (non-404) from the production-api harness base URL at the /api/generate/image/stream path would disprove that the endpoint is missing or unreachable.
A re-run of the eval that produces a generation_completed frame and imageUrlPresent=true would show the failure was transient rather than a persistent harness misconfiguration.
Evidence that SWARM_BASE_URL and LOCAL_HARNESS_URL are correctly set and point to a live, version-compatible harness would rule out a configuration error as the cause.
If other production-api checks (not just image-generation-stream) also fail with SESSION_OPEN_FAILED 404 errors, that would suggest a broader harness outage rather than a route-specific issue.
followUpEvals: Add a pre-flight harness reachability eval that verifies the production-api harness base URL returns a non-404 health or ping response before the image-generation-stream check runs, so harness connectivity failures are surfaced as a distinct check rather than surfacing as a contract assertion failure.
Add an eval that checks SWARM_BASE_URL and LOCAL_HARNESS_URL are non-empty and resolve to a live host in the production-api environment, catching misconfiguration before any stream probes execute.

Add a harness version compatibility eval that compares the running harness version against the minimum version expected by the eval runner, catching incompatible-version scenarios independently of stream content assertions.
